newsitem.title: FRANCE: French health spending down 0.4 pct in Sept vs Aug.
newsitem.headline: French health spending down 0.4 pct in Sept vs Aug.

text.p: French healthcare spending in September fell 0.4 percent versus the preceding month, the national health insurance fund, Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie (CNAM) said on Monday.

The CNAM said in a statement that the trend over the last four months considerably reduced the risk of overshooting the government target of limiting the rise in non-hospital spending to 2.1 percent this year.
But it added that the fall in spending in this area would have to continue in each of the three final months of the year to respect the target.
Curbing the rise in spending constitutes part of its efforts to reduce public deficits in preparation for European monetary union.
Spending allocated to state hospitals fell 0.3 percent and there was even greater slowdown outside that sector, the statement said.
Spending on reimbursing doctor consultation fees fell 0.5 percent in September, as in August, and versus drops of 0.3 percent in July and June, it added.
Spending on reimbursing prescriptions fell 0.4 percent versus a 0.4 percent rise in August, it said.
The statement did not provide absolute figures as it has in the past.
